evidence.intent_output: FR-HTTP-035 AC-7: an abort that an exchange reports through HttpExchange.onAbort (IR-HTTP-009) runs each res.onAbort listener once. The control (common HTTP path, HttpExecution) gives 1; the legacy dispatch path (WebSocket-upgrade request) gives 0.

findings.title: Legacy dispatch path never forwards HttpExchange.onAbort to res.abort, so res.onAbort listeners miss adapter-reported disconnects there
findings.description: Only HttpExecution.start registers exchange.onAbort(this::cancel), which calls response.abort(null). Dispatcher.handleLegacy, which builds its own DefaultResponse and runs the middleware pipeline for WebSocket-upgrade requests (and upgrade requests whose legacy lookup throws), registers nothing on the exchange. The diff covers this path for AC-4 (res.listenerLogger at line 285) but not for AC-7. A middleware that calls res.onAbort on an upgrade request never sees a disconnect that the adapter reports before the 101: the response proceeds to upgraded() and ends COMPLETED with the listener never run. The proof test shows 1 run on the common path and 0 runs on the legacy path for the same scenario.
findings.suggested_fix: In Dispatcher.handleLegacy, right after the DefaultResponse is configured, register `ex.onAbort(() -> res.abort(null));`. abort is a no-op once COMPLETED, so an abort reported after a successful 101 stays harmless. Add a regression test with an exchange that overrides onAbort, run on a ws route with an app.use middleware.

evidence.output: ex.finish() returns, then state STREAMING/COMMITTED -> COMPLETED under the lock; an abort in between sets ABORTED and runs the listeners

findings.drop_reason: Intended and documented: Response.onAbort javadoc states that an abort racing the end of a transfer, after the last byte but before completion was recorded, still ends the response aborted and runs the listener. AC-2 covers a response that completed; this window is before completion is recorded.
findings.title: An abort racing ex.finish() runs the listener on a response whose bytes all went out
findings.description: Between ex.finish() returning and the COMPLETED transition, a concurrent res.abort or an adapter-reported abort turns the response ABORTED and runs onAbort listeners.
findings.suggested_fix: None required; the behavior is the documented contract.

evidence.output: SilentExchange.clientClosed only sets a flag that the request body checks; the handler never reads the body

findings.drop_reason: The test does what AC-7 says: an exchange that keeps the SPI default onAbort, the client side closed, no listener run, and res.abort still runs it. That the core makes no I/O that could notice the close is a test-strength remark, not a defect.
findings.title: AC-7 'no detection of its own' test closes a client side that nothing reads
findings.description: The negative half of AC-7 would also pass if the core polled the socket, because the fake exchange only flips a flag.
findings.suggested_fix: Optional: have the handler read req.body() after clientClosed to show that the core reports the IOException through the error path and not as an onAbort run.

findings.drop_reason: Log message content. AC-4 only requires that the exception be logged through the app logger, and the test shows it is.
findings.title: onAbort listener failure log line has no request id
findings.description: ErrorPath logs 'request <id> failed'; the onAbort failure line has no correlation id, so a busy log is harder to read.
findings.suggested_fix: Optional: include the request id when one is set.

evidence.output: in.close() runs before the UnsupportedOperationException; a null in throws NullPointerException, and a RuntimeException from close propagates instead of the UOE

findings.drop_reason: The package is @NullMarked, so a null in breaks the contract and an NPE is the expected answer. A close() that throws RuntimeException is a broken stream. AC-2's 'throws UnsupportedOperationException' holds for every legal argument.
findings.title: Default relay throws NPE/close failure instead of UOE for illegal or broken inputs
findings.description: The default relay does not guarantee a UOE for a null or broken InputStream.

findings.drop_reason: SafeCallbacks already swallowed an Error before this change (the implementation notes rely on it), so logging an Error as well is strictly more information. No behavior AC is broken.
findings.title: Listener wrapper logs and swallows java.lang.Error, not only RuntimeException
findings.description: The javadoc names RuntimeException, but the wrapper catches Throwable, so an OutOfMemoryError or StackOverflowError from a listener is logged and swallowed on the aborting thread.
findings.suggested_fix: Optional: catch RuntimeException for logging and let SafeCallbacks handle an Error, or document that every Throwable is logged.

clean_code.description: listenerLogger lazily creates and stores a fallback SafeLogger under the response monitor, which a listener running on the aborting thread then has to take. A final default (or a volatile field set at construction) would remove the getter, the lock and the mutation.

clean_code.principle: DRY / single place of response wiring
clean_code.description: The two DefaultResponse construction sites repeat the same setter sequence (mimeTypes, resolverTap, request, applyDefaultCache, sseRegistry). The new listenerLogger call lands in HttpExecution's constructor for one site and inline in handleLegacy for the other. A shared configure step would have kept both paths aligned, and FND-001 is the kind of gap that divergence causes.
abort() and upgraded() each hand-code 'enter ABORTED, ex.abort(), abortListeners.abort() in finally'. A private helper for the abort tail would keep the listener firing rule in one place.

SilentExchange is about 100 lines of hand delegation to RecordingExchange, kept private to one test. A testFixtures delegating exchange, or a java.lang.reflect.Proxy over HttpExchange, would serve the next test that needs an SPI onAbort-reporting exchange.
DefaultResponse is now 1140 lines and mixes header policy, body framing, transfer copy, SSE, WebSocket upgrade end-state and now abort-listener bookkeeping with logger fallback.
